note: assumptions register and negative results (D-068); built only from committed results files by notebooks/40_assumptions_and_reality.ipynb; no simulation, no grid data; every number is read from the file and JSON pointer in its provenance_id
evidence_scope: validation (selection) results; the sealed test window [2025-11-01, 2026-11-01) is never read

register.assumption: Flexible-job share, and every flexible job may move
register.value_text: 41.8% of jobs and 46.1% of GPU-hours are flexible (half of the Pretrain/SFT/MLLM/Eval candidates, by a seeded hash); mobile = flexible
register.used_in: every policy: which jobs may wait or move
register.reality: Large multi-node jobs are tied to their site by data, checkpoints and interconnect (data gravity); few real fleets could move them freely.
register.result_text: Mobility ≤ 8 GPUs: W saves 3.9% [2.6, 5.4] against the primary 22.5% [18.4, 26.7]. The no-flexible and all-candidates-flexible runs were cut (D-058).

register.assumption: Spare GPU slots at each destination (CISO, BPAT, NEVP)
register.used_in: every moving policy (S, K, W, L, H)
register.reality: Spare remote capacity is not a standing reservation: it varies by hour, and the cleanest sites are the ones everyone else wants too.

register.assumption: Transfer before a remote run: time and energy
register.value_text: 30 min and 5% of the job's IT energy
register.used_in: every remote run: deadline slack and transfer CO₂
register.reality: Staging a multi-terabyte dataset or checkpoint can take hours; no dataset size or network power was measured.
register.result_text: 120 min: S saves 20.2% [16.6, 23.7] (primary S 22.6% [18.4, 26.8]). Transfer energy 0% and 20% was cut (D-058).

register.assumption: Active IT power per GPU slot
register.used_in: all energy and CO₂; the storage site connection
register.reality: Real draw varies with the GPU generation and with utilisation; it was not measured.
register.result_text: Not run: the 0.40 and 0.80 kW runs were cut (D-058). Every kWh and tonne scales with it, so the saving fractions do not change in this model; the storage connection limit (2,288 slots × kW × PUE) does.

register.reality: PUE differs by site and climate and rises in hot weather; one value for all sites is a simplification.
register.result_text: Not run: remote PUE 1.10 and 1.56 was cut (D-058); temperature-dependent PUE is future work (D-063).

register.value_text: every job holds its U booking as a fallback (F11; assumed)
register.used_in: every policy: what a job may displace
register.reality: A real router does not know future jobs' bookings; the result is an advance-reservation scenario, not an online router, and zero deadline misses hold by construction.
register.result_text: Not run: the 'possible without advance reservations' sensitivity (shadow U) was cut by the owner (D-058). The bookings' effect on the saving is not signed.

register.value_text: realized runtime = declared runtime (known at arrival)
register.reality: Jobs overrun or end early, and declared budgets are rarely exact.
register.result_text: Not run: the +25% runtime-overrun stress was cut (D-058).

register.value_text: Seren 161-day cycle at phase 0 (simulated arrivals; measured durations and GPU counts): 435,833 source attempts, 5.4 M GPU-hours per cycle
register.used_in: the whole experiment: arrivals, sizes, durations
register.reality: Seren is one AI lab's trace on another continent's clock; a Utah cluster's job mix, sizes and timing would differ.
register.result_text: Phase 49 days: S saves 23.2% [18.9, 27.6]; phase 98: 22.0% [18.1, 26.5] (primary S 22.6% [18.4, 26.8]). Civil-time (DST) alignment was cut (D-058).

register.value_text: EIA's estimated hourly consumption-basis CO₂ intensity (an average, attributed)
register.reality: Attributed average intensity is not the CO₂ a moved job physically changes; on the margin the gain can be far smaller (notebook 05).
register.result_text: Production basis (same schedules): S saves 25.5% [20.8, 30.1], against 22.6% [18.4, 26.8] on the consumption basis. A flat marginal factor is tested on storage (§2).

register.used_in: the dashboard's carbon colour scale only
register.reality: It is a national, annual, generation-basis average; the hourly consumption-basis values it colours are on a different basis.
register.result_text: Not tested: a display reference only; no result depends on it (D-055).

register.assumption: Storage round-trip efficiency and the site connection limit
register.value_text: η 0.85; charging limited by a 1.65 MW connection
register.used_in: the illustrative storage piece only (not the scheduler)
register.reality: Real batteries also lose energy to self-discharge, auxiliaries and ageing (ignored here), and a site connection can be upgraded.
register.result_text: At 4 MWh, fixed schedule: cut 2.0% at η 0.75, 3.5% at η 0.85, 4.2% at η 0.9; connection +25%: 4.5%. Average basis; on a flat marginal factor it adds CO₂ (§2).

register.value_text: PACE net load ≥ the training years' 99% quantile (7,207 MW): 12 validation hours
register.used_in: peak relief and the storage rush view
register.reality: Stress is not one net-load threshold; operators' tight hours depend on reserves, imports and outages.
register.result_text: Quantile sweep: 95% → 269 hours, W changes the cluster's PACE load by −0.29 MW; 98% → 67 hours, W changes the cluster's PACE load by −0.29 MW; 99% → 12 hours, W changes the cluster's PACE load by −0.25 MW, against a PACE net-load peak of 8,173 MW.

register.assumption: Water: whether hydro reservoir evaporation counts
register.value_text: generation water from NREL median factors × the EIA-930 fuel mix, without and with hydro evaporation (illustrative)
register.reality: Evaporation from a reservoir serves many uses, and NREL's hydro range spans 13×; allocating it to power is a choice, and it decides the sign.
register.result_text: S without hydro: −20.5%; with hydro evaporation: +145.4% against U (§2).

negative_results.title: Waiting in Utah barely helps
negative_results.statement: Time-only routers that may only wait in PACE save 0.7% [0.5, 0.9] (W_time) and 0.7% [0.6, 1.0] (L_time); moving saves 22.5% [18.3, 26.6] (L).

negative_results.title: A carbon-blind router saves about nothing
negative_results.statement: G (earliest finish across sites, no carbon input) saves 0.010% [0.000, 0.022].

negative_results.title: H2 inconclusive: the learned forecast does not beat the weekly one
negative_results.statement: W − L = −0.16 t [−8.8, +7.2] (positive = L emits less); direction: inconclusive.

negative_results.title: H3 not supported: no dynamic search beats the fixed ranking
negative_results.statement: S − K = −10.0 t [−19.3, −1.5]: K emits more than S, and the interval excludes zero. S − W = −4.9 t [−14.8, +3.6] and S − L = −5.1 t [−15.3, +4.2]: not distinguishable from S.

negative_results.title: If only small jobs can move, most of the saving is gone
negative_results.statement: With moves limited to jobs of 8 GPUs or fewer, W saves 3.9% [2.6, 5.4], against 22.5% [18.4, 26.7] when every flexible job may move.

negative_results.title: No remote capacity: S does nothing
negative_results.statement: With 0 destination slots, S saves 0.0% [0.0, 0.0]; the best router left is a time-only one (W 0.7% [0.5, 0.9]).

negative_results.title: Storage adds CO₂ on a flat marginal factor
negative_results.statement: At 4 MWh, η 0.85, fixed schedule: storage cuts 164 t on hourly average intensity, but on a flat 618 g/kWh marginal factor (an associational regression slope, R² 0.47) it changes CO₂ by +109 t (its losses).

negative_results.title: Peak relief is tiny at Utah's scale
negative_results.statement: In the rush hours, W lowers the cluster's PACE load by 0.25 MW against U; PACE's net-load peak is 8,173 MW, so the relief is 0.0031% of it.

negative_results.title: The production basis would flatter hydro
negative_results.statement: Priced on production-basis intensity, the same S schedules save 25.5% [20.8, 30.1], more than the 22.6% [18.4, 26.8] on the consumption basis we report: hydro-heavy BPAT generates cleaner power than its loads consume.

negative_results.title: The literal illustrative-job rule picks a 3-minute job
negative_results.statement: The §11 rule (nearest the median GPU-hours) picks a 1-GPU, 203 s job, because short jobs dominate the trace; the story shows the GPU-hour-weighted median job instead.

negative_results.title: Water: an assumption decides the sign (illustrative)
negative_results.statement: Counting only power-plant cooling water, S changes generation water by −0.6 M gal (−20%) against U. Counting hydro reservoir evaporation, S, W and L use 2.4–2.5× as much as U (+5.2 to +5.5 M gal), and NREL's hydro factor spans 13×.

weather.statement: H is the same reservation search as K, W and L, given the realised carbon instead of a forecast. It is what a perfect forecast would give this router, not an upper bound: a greedy search is not a cohort optimum. Perfect carbon foresight (H) saves 22.6% [18.4, 26.8] against U; the fixed clean-region ranking S saves 22.6% [18.4, 26.8]. S − H = −0.5 t [−9.9, +8.0]: H does not beat S. H does beat the weekly forecast W, by W − H = +4.5 t [+2.3, +6.9] (0.12% of W's CO₂), that is what a perfect forecast adds to this search, and S, with no forecast at all, is not distinguishable from H. Only 29% of flexible energy has its deadline inside issued forecast coverage at every legal site, so most decisions rest on the tail climatology, not on the forecast.
weather.conclusion: In this setup even perfect carbon foresight does not beat a fixed ranking, so weather-informed forecasts are unlikely to change the routing result. They may matter for peak-stress forecasting, which we did not evaluate; the most a perfect forecast adds here is about 0.1% of W's CO₂.
